scores.thesis: World-class consumer ecosystem moat (hardware + services lock-in), ~$100B+ annual FCF, elite capital returns via buybacks, and pricing power. However, at a ~$4.6T market cap a 100x outcome (~$460T) would exceed world GDP — mathematically implausible. This is a core quality compounder, not a satellite hundred-bagger candidate.
catalysts: AI-driven iPhone upgrade cycle via Apple Intelligence
Services mix expansion and monetization (payments, ads, health)
Ongoing mega-buybacks shrinking share count
New categories (Vision-class spatial computing, wearables/health)
risks: Antitrust/regulatory pressure (App Store, Google TAC payments)
China manufacturing and demand concentration
Perceived AI execution lag vs. peers
Mature smartphone market limits unit growth
scores.pass_reason: Mandate mismatch: $4.6T starting market cap makes 100x implausible; belongs in a core quality sleeve, not a 100x satellite allocation.

scores.thesis: Premier enterprise franchise with deep moats across cloud (Azure), productivity (M365), and AI distribution (Copilot/OpenAI), generating very high ROIC and recurring revenue. At ~$3.7T market cap, 100x (~$370T) is impossible; a superb core holding but not a hundred-bagger satellite name.
catalysts: Azure AI workload growth and capacity coming online
Copilot monetization across the enterprise installed base
Margin leverage as AI revenue scales
OpenAI ecosystem optionality
risks: Massive AI capex pressuring near-term FCF and returns on invested capital
Cloud competition (AWS, Google Cloud)
Antitrust scrutiny of bundling and OpenAI ties
Dependence on partner model quality (OpenAI)
scores.pass_reason: $3.7T market cap precludes 100x; fits core compounding allocation, not the hundred-bagger mandate.

scores.thesis: Greatest capital-allocation track record ever, fortress balance sheet with ~$300B+ cash, and a diversified insurance/industrial/energy engine. But at ~$1.0T it is a GDP-plus compounder with structural size drag and a looming succession transition. Zero plausible 100x path from here.
catalysts: Deployment of record cash pile into a large acquisition
Insurance float and underwriting profit growth
Buybacks if valuation compresses
Energy/infrastructure investment runway (BHE)
risks: Key-man/succession risk (Buffett age; Abel transition)
Cash drag in an elevated market
Size structurally caps forward returns
Insurance catastrophe loss exposure
scores.pass_reason: ~$1T conglomerate cannot 100x; suitable as core defensive ballast, not a satellite moonshot.

scores.thesis: Genuinely massive TAM: direct-to-device satellite broadband targeting billions of under-connected mobile users via a capital-light wholesale model with MNO partners (AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten). First-mover moat in spectrum rights and large-aperture BlueBird satellite design. But heavy capex, repeated dilution, unproven unit economics, and Starlink direct-to-cell competition — plus a $28B starting valuation — make 100x implausible; a multi-bagger at best.
catalysts: Commercial service activation with AT&T/Verizon and first revenue scaling
FCC/regulatory approvals including supplemental coverage from space (SCS)
Constellation build-out and launch cadence proving manufacturing scale
Government/defense contract wins and MNO partner expansion
risks: Ongoing dilution and capex funding needs before FCF breakeven
Launch or satellite deployment failures
SpaceX Starlink direct-to-cell competitive overlap
Execution delays and premium valuation already pricing in success

scores.thesis: Best-run pure-play space company: Electron dominates dedicated small launch, Space Systems is scaling fast with vertical integration, and Neutron could open the medium-lift market — a real end-to-end space platform moat with strong execution. However, the ~$50B market cap already discounts substantial success; 100x (~$5T) is implausible. Attractive multi-bagger profile, not a hundred bagger.
catalysts: Neutron first launch and commercial/national security ramp
Record Electron cadence and reusability milestones
Large Space Systems/SDA and defense constellation contract wins
Path toward sustained profitability and positive FCF
risks: Neutron development delays or launch anomaly
Cash burn and potential dilution funding Neutron
SpaceX price/ride-share competition
Rich valuation vulnerable to any execution slip

scores.thesis: Leading pure-play on the emerging lunar economy with NASA CLPS delivery missions and a lunar data/navigation (NSNS) ambition — real first-mover positioning. But revenue is lumpy and NASA-concentrated, missions carry binary risk, and dilution is persistent. At ~$3.6B it is one of the smaller names here, yet 100x (~$360B) would exceed the plausible size of the entire lunar services market for decades.
catalysts: Successful IM lunar missions demonstrating repeatable delivery
New CLPS/NASA award wins and Artemis program funding momentum
Commercialization of lunar data relay/navigation services
Potential strategic partnerships or M&A interest
risks: Mission failure risk on any given landing
Heavy dependence on NASA budgets and contract timing
Lumpy, low-visibility revenue; ongoing share dilution
Competition (Firefly, Astrobotic, international programs)

scores.thesis: Space infrastructure and components roll-up with exposure to civil, national security, and commercial space growth — picks-and-shovels angle on a growing market. But it carries integration risk, leverage, thin margins, and a history of dilution and execution stumbles. 100x (~$320B) would make it larger than today's largest defense primes — not plausible.
catalysts: National security space budget growth and program wins
Margin expansion from scale and integration synergies
Accretive bolt-on M&A in space components
Microgravity/biotech (PIL-BOX) optionality
risks: M&A integration and goodwill impairment risk
Leverage and lumpy government contract revenue
Competitive pressure across component markets
Dilution history and inconsistent profitability

scores.thesis: Independent voice-AI pure play with real traction in restaurant drive-thru/ordering and automotive assistants; the agentic/voice AI TAM is large and its independence appeals to brands avoiding big-tech platforms. But it competes against hyperscaler voice/LLM offerings, remains unprofitable with ongoing dilution, and 100x (~$350B) would require becoming one of the world's largest software companies — implausible.
catalysts: Enterprise restaurant chain rollouts at scale
Automotive design wins converting to production revenue
Agentic AI expansion into new verticals (healthcare, financial services)
Path to adjusted EBITDA breakeven
risks: Competition/commoditization from OpenAI, Google, Amazon voice stacks
Cash burn and recurring equity dilution
Customer concentration and long sales cycles
Extreme valuation volatility typical of AI small caps

scores.thesis: Trapped-ion quantum computing leader with industry-best gate fidelities and a credible networking roadmap; optionality is enormous if fault-tolerant quantum arrives. But current revenues are tiny relative to a ~$17.7B valuation, the technical timeline to commercial advantage is uncertain, and 100x (~$1.8T) is not credible. A speculative multi-bagger lottery ticket, not a hundred bagger.
catalysts: New system generations and algorithmic-qubit milestones
Quantum networking expansion and government/defense contracts
Enterprise/cloud adoption via AWS, Azure, Google partnerships
Acquisitions consolidating quantum talent and IP
risks: Uncertain path and timeline to fault-tolerant, commercially useful quantum
Intense competition (IBM, Google, Quantinuum, PsiQuantum)
Heavy cash burn and dilution against minimal revenue
Valuation highly sensitive to technical roadmap slippage

scores.thesis: eVTOL frontrunner with the deepest FAA certification progress, a vertically integrated manufacturing model, and strong strategic backing (Toyota, Delta) plus early Dubai launch rights. The urban air mobility TAM is theoretically large, but the company is pre-revenue, unit economics are unproven, infrastructure is nascent, and 100x (~$850B) is implausible from an ~$8.5B base.
catalysts: FAA type certification milestones and final approval
Dubai commercial service launch and first passenger revenue
Toyota manufacturing scale-up and funding support
US market entry (NYC/LA) and DoD contract expansion
risks: Certification delays pushing out revenue
Cash burn and dilution before breakeven
Unproven demand, pricing, and unit economics for air taxis
Safety incident risk and competition (Archer, Wisk, EHang)
